coverage: Pinned Isaac rigid-body state and applied wrenches

findings.finding: Rotor thrust, moment arms and alternating reaction torque provide an explicit actuation model for the existing controller. Isaac exposes rigid-body state and applied wrenches; its pinned Lab 3 convention must be used instead of assuming older APIs.
findings.relevance: Simulation-only drone flight-control development with inspectable 3D physics results
findings.direction_alignment: The maintainer explicitly requested further drone development grounded in physics and 3D visualization.
findings.opportunity_or_risk: Actuator coupling and delay expose control behavior absent from the ideal-wrench baseline; incorrect frame conversion can reverse the response.
findings.engineering_cost: One rotor/Isaac control slice, versioned evidence support and reuse of the existing 3D viewer
findings.roadmap_delta: AL-006: rotor-actuated native flight control in Isaac with local 3D replay
findings.verification_needed: Mixer/lag tests, recorded actual PhysX trials, strict actuator evidence checks and browser verification

overall_recommendation: Implement the approved rotor-control slice with the existing pinned simulator and gains; retain the CPU and learned-policy baselines.
evidence_gaps: Rotor-actuated closed-loop PhysX trials and their 3D replay are not yet validated.
Example actuator parameters are not hardware identification results.
